title: Fair warning
screen: Fair warning. → Selling an elephant takes time. → Almost 6 minutes. (☕ ☕) → You can't rush an elephant. → Worth it.
voice: Fair warning: selling an elephant is not a quick business. Elephants take their time. So does this video: six and a half minutes. Yes, six and a half. Grab a coffee. Maybe two. You can't rush an elephant. Believe us, we tried. We promise the elephant is worth it.

title: Details
screen: (All-caps headings · Walls of text · Posters screen readers can't read · Naked links · Random fonts and colours · Staff who left years ago) → Each one looks like a detail. → Together, they make a good school look worse than it is. → Now multiply it. ×100 ×200 ×500 ×1 000
voice: Here are twelve mistakes that catch the eye the most. Each mistake looks like a detail. Together, they make a good school look worse than it is. Now multiply it by a hundred schools. Two hundred. Five hundred… and more.

title: The only channel you control
screen: Not mandatory where you are? → The only channel a school controls. → Not image. Relevance.
voice: Maybe websites aren't mandatory where you are. They will matter anyway. A website is the only channel a school fully controls. Search engines read it. AI answers are built from it. Agents will act on it. What matters is not how it looks, but whether it's current.

title: Each school alone
screen: The elephant in the room. → Same duties. Each school alone. → Quality becomes a matter of chance.
voice: Let's address the elephant in the room. Every school has the same duties: accessibility, data protection, security, and rules that keep changing. Most face them alone, with their own budget and their own contractor. So quality comes down to chance.

title: Stumps
screen: A new website every few years? → continuity lost → Stop replacing. Start growing.
voice: And every few years: a new tender, a new website. The tree is cut back to a stump and planted again. And again. Each time, continuity is lost. Ours is never cut down. Wind bent it, rain soaked it: every new rule, every change. It only grew stronger. And now nobody argues that it was worth it.

title: Only the surface
screen: Shared digital infrastructure for schools. → The website is only the surface.
voice: Cleverphant is shared digital infrastructure for schools. What people see is the website. Underneath is everything that keeps it right, from one design system to compliance and support, shared by every school. A new school simply plugs in.

title: Design system
voice: What is a design system? A set of ready-made parts. Colours, fonts and buttons make blocks: a search field, a staff card. Blocks make sections, sections make pages. Every page of every school is built from the same parts, and every part already meets accessibility rules: contrast, headings, keyboard. Improve one part once, and it improves everywhere.
screen: What is a design system? → Parts → Blocks → Sections → Pages → Every page, from the same parts. (Contrast · Headings · Keyboard) → Improve one part. Every page improves.

title: No blank page
voice: Some see us as an agency. Others, as yet another do-it-yourself website builder. We are neither: we are a platform with a human touch. Nobody starts from a blank page: we move the old website for the school, its pages, documents and staff profiles, cleaned up on the way. We ask the school a few clarifying questions and to fill in what is missing. Not much work, but the school's part matters. The school checks, and the new website goes live.
screen: Not an agency. Not a builder. Software with a human touch. → No blank page. We move it, and clean it on the way.

title: One notices
screen: Same benefit. Same bug. (it happens) → One school notices. Every school is fixed. → Knowledge travels the same way. (Lesson · Video · Newsletter)
voice: Because every school runs on the same system, they all get the same benefits... And yes... the same bugs. It happens. But it takes just one school to notice. Fixed once, fixed for all. The same goes for knowledge. When one school asks a question, the answer becomes a lesson, a video and a newsletter for every school.

title: Pilot → standard
screen: Ideas travel the same way. → Pilot: slow. Standard: everyone, at once.
voice: Ideas travel the same way. An innovative school leader brings a need. Their school becomes the pilot. Slow. Very slow. Then the data shows it works, and every school has it at once.

title: Publish once
screen: Publish once. → Reach every school. (No emails · No reminders · No school left behind) → A big network can afford big ideas.
voice: And it can work from the top, too. What is common to every school is updated once: accessibility, update subscriptions, cookies. It appears on every school website at the same time. No emails. No reminders. None left out. Distribution is already solved. So a big network can afford big ideas: things no single school could ever build alone, built once and shared by all.

title: Equally good
screen: Quality shouldn't depend on size. → Not identical. Equally good.
voice: A small village school gets what a large city school gets. One design system underneath; the face stays the school's own. Not identical. Equally good.

title: Trojan elephant
screen: Change starts with details. → One bite at a time. → Every step lands on every school.
voice: Change starts with details. Being small is no excuse to look away. Elephants are slow. Very slow. So slow that nobody notices the change, until it's everywhere. That's our Trojan elephant. How do you eat an elephant? One bite at a time. Today the headings. Tomorrow the cookie banner. The day after, document names. No single bite looks like a reform. A year later, the school is different. And every next step lands on every school: live tables, whistleblower channels, consultation booking, surveys, event calendars, weekly update digests.

title: What if…
screen: What if…? → One school pilots it. Every school gets it.
voice: And we keep asking: what if? What if a teacher's Word file became a finished article? What if documents named and filed themselves? What if a fix was ready before you saw the problem? None of this needs a new website. Each idea is an app on the same foundation. One school pilots it, every school gets it.

title: And AI?
voice: And AI? Not another chatbot. AI that quietly keeps things in order. Because AI loves order.

title: The logic of scale
screen: What works in one school works everywhere. → Not a promise of cheap. The logic of scale.
voice: What works in one school works in a municipality, a region, a whole country. Schools can be added quickly, while costs grow far more slowly. Not a promise of cheap. The logic of scale.

title: Walked this road
screen: 15 years. The first ten? Slow. → Skip the slow part. → The goal: giving teachers back to their students. → almost 300 institutions · 51 of 60 municipalities → Built in Lithuania. Ready for yours. → Same rules across the EU. Built for one, ready for all.
voice: We have walked this road for fifteen years. The first ten? Slow. Very slow. So slow. Change in schools takes time. Then the network started to grow by itself. Today: almost three hundred institutions on one standard, with at least one client in eighty-five percent of Lithuania's municipalities. You don't have to start from the slow part. Audits, onboarding and training are ready. And an elephant never forgets: when staff change, the knowledge stays. The goal was never the websites. It is giving teachers back to their students. Built in a small country. Ready for yours. Across the European Union, public institutions share the same rules: web accessibility, data protection, whistleblower protection. Built for one, ready for all. Let's talk about your region.
